fields.text: A vision model surveys a room photo and splits it into architecture that must not move and everything that may change. An LLM designer plans a makeover that respects that keep-list, a second LLM turns the plan into a surgical edit instruction, and Muse Edit renders the redesign from the original photo. A Decide judge then audits the render against the plan and labels it faithful redesign, minor drift, architecture moved or barely changed - the redesign has to answer to the survey. Four model families, four different jobs. See recipes/room-makeover-audit.md.

nodes.name: Room makeover, audited - survey, design, render, audit

fields.text: Redesign as a warm Scandinavian living room: pale cream walls, light oak, sage and rust accents, natural woven textiles, soft warm evening light. Cosmetic changes only, sensible mid-range budget, keep the room's layout and function as a living room. No structural work.

fields.q: You are the surveyor in an interior-redesign pipeline. Look at this photo of a room and write a survey in two sections. Section 1, headed 'KEEP EXACTLY:', lists the architecture that must not move or change shape: every window and door with its wall and rough position, the ceiling and any beams, the floor footprint, and the camera viewpoint. Section 2, headed 'CHANGEABLE:', lists the furniture, decor, colours, finishes and lighting that could change, each with its position in the room. List ONLY what you can actually see, with no redesign suggestions and no invented dimensions. If you are unsure of an item, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'.

fields.system: You are an interior designer. The input gives a redesign brief first, then a survey of a room in two sections: KEEP EXACTLY (architecture) and CHANGEABLE (furniture, decor, finishes). Write ONE redesign plan in this exact shape: a title line naming the style; a 'Keep exactly:' line that repeats the survey's architecture items, shortened if needed but never dropped or altered; then a 'Changes:' list of 5 to 8 concrete changes drawn ONLY from the CHANGEABLE items - new colours, finishes, textiles, furniture styles and lighting that deliver the brief. No structural changes, no moved, added or removed windows or doors, no new furniture positions that block a door or window. Output the plan only, no preamble.

You write ONE edit instruction for an image editor, from a redesign plan. The editor receives the original room photo. Your instruction must: start with 'Keep exactly:' followed by the plan's architecture list in compressed form, including the same camera viewpoint; then describe the planned changes concretely (colours, materials, furniture, textiles, lighting); end with 'Photorealistic, same room, no people, no text.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the instruction only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Redesigned room - Muse Edit renders it

fields.question: The text is a redesign plan for a room; its 'Keep exactly:' line lists the architecture that must not move. The image is a rendered redesign that claims to follow that plan. Which verdict fits? 'faithful redesign' means the architecture and camera viewpoint are unchanged AND most planned changes are visibly applied. 'minor drift' means it is clearly the same room with the style applied, but a small architectural detail or one planned change is off. 'architecture moved' means a window, door, ceiling or the camera viewpoint changed materially, or it is effectively a different room. 'barely changed' means the architecture is intact but most planned changes were not applied - it still looks like the original room. Judge the room, not the photography.
fields.options:
faithful redesign
minor drift
architecture moved
barely changed
